investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-01T20:15–20:23Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval runner could not advance past the createAgent call.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for a new peer-pod VM. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885 (createAgent call) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving zero schedulable capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), indicating all existing peer-pod slots are occupied by non-preemptible workloads.

Secondary: The node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata-capable nodes), and those nodes are saturated. If the affinity were broadened or additional kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling could succeed.

Tertiary: A resource leak or runaway agent lifecycle may have left peer-pod VMs allocated but not released, consuming the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota without active use. This would explain why preemption found no victims.

Lower confidence: A cluster scaling event (node removal, maintenance drain) may have reduced the number of kata-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent probe traffic, but no node-event evidence is present in the packet.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the scheduler message changed to a different error (e.g., image pull failure, OOMKilled, API auth error) on a re-run, the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened.

If the eval passed on a re-run without any infrastructure change, the failure would be transient (e.g., a briefly occupied slot was released) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If only one of the three sibling checks reproduced the scheduler message while others passed, the failure would be localized to a specific probe invocation rather than a cluster-wide capacity problem.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined on any node (i.e., the resource class was removed), the root cause would be a missing resource registration rather than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries the cluster for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity and fails with a warning before slots are fully exhausted, providing earlier signal than a pod scheduling timeout.

Add a check that detects stuck or leaked remote agent pods (pods in Pending/Unschedulable state for more than a configurable threshold) and reports them as a separate evidence item, distinct from the agent creation check itself.

Consider a shorter timeout sentinel check for remote agent pod schedulability (e.g., fail fast at 30s with a distinct 'capacity' message) so the eval framework can distinguish scheduling failures from agent runtime failures more precisely.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted by the eval runner was left unschedulable for ~142–145 seconds. The Kubernetes scheduler reported that only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to help. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the remote agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any of the required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes. With 0 available VM slots and no preemption victims, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. The eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returns a live agent, so the probe times out and emits zero evidence, violating the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure scoped to the remote-agents Swarm/kata-peerpods node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact is unconfirmed.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-01T20:15–20:23Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval runner could not advance past the createAgent call.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for a new peer-pod VM. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885 (createAgent call) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving zero schedulable capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), indicating all existing peer-pod slots are occupied by non-preemptible workloads.

Secondary: The node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata-capable nodes), and those nodes are saturated. If the affinity were broadened or additional kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling could succeed.

Tertiary: A resource leak or runaway agent lifecycle may have left peer-pod VMs allocated but not released, consuming the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota without active use. This would explain why preemption found no victims.

Lower confidence: A cluster scaling event (node removal, maintenance drain) may have reduced the number of kata-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent probe traffic, but no node-event evidence is present in the packet.

Add a cleanup-verification eval step that confirms no remote-agent pods from the previous run are still present before starting a new probe cycle.
Add a node-pool health check eval that verifies at least one node satisfies the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector and has available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity.

Add a latency-band eval assertion: if pod scheduling takes longer than a configurable threshold (e.g., 30s), emit a warning evidence key so the failure is caught earlier than the full outageLatencyMs timeout.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM workload: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm runtime has exhausted available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) is identical across all three checks, confirming the failure is a shared infrastructure scheduling constraint rather than an application-layer or eval-runner defect. The eval runner branch in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with type "remote" (line 1918), which triggers the kata peer-pod VM allocation that the cluster cannot satisfy. No evidence of a user-facing incident or real-traffic impact is present in the packet; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity condition.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 145s before the eval timed out.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=153080, status=fail, endedAt=2026-07-01T20:23:09.051Z — the check ran for ~153 seconds, well past the 145s unschedulable window, confirming the pod never became ready.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message was ever returned, consistent with the agent pod never starting.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, matching the contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 266-270.

sibling.remote-agent-create: same scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), latencyMs=148594, endedAt=2026-07-01T20:18:07.234Z — failed before remote-agent-runtime was even attempted.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same scheduler error, latencyMs=148737, endedAt=2026-07-01T20:20:35.971Z — failed sequentially after remote-agent-create.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the call that triggers kata peer-pod VM allocation.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the check failed at 153080ms, well within the outage threshold, but all three checks failing means the feature's degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 thresholds are both breached by the two required sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state).
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or leaked/stuck pods from prior eval runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at capacity, making the effective schedulable pool size 0.

Tertiary — a stuck or zombie kata peer-pod from a previous eval run (e.g., a cleanup failure in withCleanup) is holding a VM slot on one or both eligible nodes, preventing new pods from being scheduled.

Lower probability — the 2 kata-capable nodes are in a degraded or NotReady state that the scheduler reports as insufficient rather than unavailable, which would appear identically in the scheduler message.

affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 eligible nodes, making this the primary failing boundary (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents swarm runtime — agent pod provisioning
affectedAreas.reason: The eval runner calls createAgent with type 'remote' (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), which depends on kata peer-pod VM allocation. All three remote-agent checks fail at this boundary.

The check is registered as required=false (infra/evals/status/features.json line 185) but its failure, combined with the two required sibling failures, breaches the feature's outageAfterFailures=2 threshold.

affectedAreas.reason: All 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) defined at lines 266-270 are missing because the agent pod never started, so no contract assertion could be evaluated.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the Kubernetes cluster for pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots in the remote-agents scheduling namespace — identify and terminate any stuck or zombie pods from prior eval runs to free capacity.

Check the 2 kata-capable nodes' current allocatable vs. requested kata.peerpods.io/vm resource counts to determine whether the cluster is at hard capacity or whether leaked pods are the proximate cause.

Review the withCleanup function in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm that remote agent pods are reliably deleted on eval timeout or error; if not, add a guaranteed cleanup path to prevent VM slot leaks across eval runs.

If the cluster is at hard capacity (no leaked pods), evaluate whether additional kata-capable nodes need to be provisioned or whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node needs to be increased to support concurrent eval runs.
Monitor whether the failure is transient (resolves on next scheduled run) or persistent (repeats), as this distinguishes a momentary capacity spike from a structural under-provisioning problem.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false (infra/evals/status/features.json line 185), but the two required sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) are both failing, which means the feature's outageAfterFailures=2 threshold is already breached — treat this as a feature-level outage signal for the remote-agents feature, not just a non-critical check failure.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is persistent or transient. A pass would indicate the capacity issue resolved itself; a fail with the same message confirms ongoing exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Querying the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity will show whether kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are fully consumed and by which pods, directly confirming or refuting the exhaustion hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies any stuck or zombie eval pods from prior runs that may be holding VM slots, which would confirm the leaked-pod sub-hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect implicated source paths for cleanup logic
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Review infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs around the withCleanup function to determine whether cleanup of remote agent pods is guaranteed on timeout or error, which would explain whether leaked pods are a recurring risk.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three remote-agents sibling checks together after any cluster remediation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Validates that all three checks recover together after VM capacity is restored, confirming the shared scheduling dependency.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes nodes show available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (i.e., allocatable > requested) at the time of the failure, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduling constraint must be investigated.
If the scheduler message changes to a different error (e.g., image pull failure, OOM, or API auth error) on a re-run after no cluster changes, the kata VM capacity explanation would be weakened.
If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass on a re-run, the failure is isolated to the runtime eval path rather than a shared scheduling constraint.
If a cluster-level event log shows the 2 kata-capable nodes were in NotReady or SchedulingDisabled state at 2026-07-01T20:18–20:23Z, the cause is node availability rather than VM slot exhaustion.

If the withCleanup function in run-status-probes.mjs successfully terminates all prior eval pods and the next run passes without any cluster changes, the root cause is a leaked pod holding a VM slot rather than true capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity before attempting remote agent creation, and emits a dedicated 'kata-vm-capacity' evidence field — this would surface exhaustion before the pod scheduling timeout is reached.
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote-agent eval pods remain in Pending or Running state after each probe run, catching VM slot leaks before they affect subsequent runs.

Add a historical trend eval that tracks remote-agent check latency across runs — a latency approaching the 142-145s unschedulable window on multiple consecutive runs would be an early warning of capacity pressure before full exhaustion.
Consider a dedicated 'remote-agent-node-affinity' eval that verifies the count of kata-capable nodes matches the expected minimum, alerting when the schedulable pool shrinks below a safe threshold.
